headline: Running streak ties its all-time high as volume holds flat and a fresh lactate threshold test anchors current aerobic fitness at 4:24/km.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Volume has been almost perfectly stable across the last eight weeks — 127 km this block versus 125 km prior, with identical run counts — so there's no meaningful load change to interpret. What matters more is how that volume is distributed: the 15.73 km effort at 4:49/km on June 27 stands out as the quality anchor of the recent block, with HR at 161 and a load of 239, well above anything else in the past fortnight. The two easy runs either side of it (13.77 km at 5:48 and 11.73 km at 5:59) look like appropriate bookends rather than lost fitness.

The lactate threshold test on July 2 gives you a concrete number to work with: 4:24/km at 178 bpm. Set against your half-marathon PB pace of 4:18/km and your 10K PB pace of 4:12/km, that positions your threshold in a plausible range for your current fitness. As the 30-day baseline accumulates more tests, this single data point will become more useful — for now, treat it as a calibration marker rather than a definitive trend.

Easy-run HR is tracking notably lower than the prior comparison period — averaging 147 bpm versus 157 bpm across six comparable-effort runs in each window. That's a meaningful shift in the aerobic direction at similar paces, and it's the strongest internal signal in the current data. Whether it reflects genuine aerobic adaptation, favourable conditions, or slightly reduced effort is worth watching across the coming weeks, but at face value it's a positive indicator.

The 20-week streak ties your personal best, which is worth noting not as a milestone but as evidence of structural consistency. Strength volume dropped to 4 sessions this block from 6 prior — not alarming given the run quality and overall load, but worth tracking if it extends another block.
